title: Docs: Add AWS Marketplace onboarding page + FAQ; link from pricing & getting-started
creator: Elliot Price
description:
## Summary
Create a customer-facing AWS Marketplace onboarding page on the docs site, plus a short FAQ section focused on procurement + activation. Ensure the new page is discoverable via links from (1) Pricing/Packaging and (2) Getting Started.

This is part of the Cloud Marketplace Listing Refresh project (AWS + GCP). The goal is to reduce "purchase → activated" time and lower support tickets for entitlement lag / org linking confusion.

## Target audience
- Enterprise buyers and platform teams purchasing via AWS Marketplace
- Solutions Engineers / Customer Success sending a single canonical link to prospects
- Procurement/security reviewers looking for process + responsibilities (not deep product docs)

## Requirements
### Page location + nav
- Add docs page: **/marketplace/aws** (final slug can be /docs/marketplace/aws depending on site routing conventions)
- Add to left nav under a "Marketplace" or "Billing & Procurement" section (coordinate with Docs IA owner)
- Add prominent links from:
  - Pricing page ("Buy via AWS Marketplace" section)
  - Getting Started / onboarding overview ("Purchased via AWS Marketplace? Start here")

### Content (AWS-specific)
Include:
1) **Prerequisites**
   - Redwood org needed (or user will create org during linking)
   - Admin permissions: ability to accept/subscribe in AWS Marketplace + access to Redwood Console
   - Info to have handy: AWS account ID, subscribed product/SKU name (if relevant), desired region

2) **Purchase steps (AWS Marketplace)**
   - Subscribe in AWS Marketplace
   - Confirm selected plan/SKU (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; add-ons if applicable)
   - Call out that AWS subscription does not automatically create a Redwood org; you must link

3) **Activation / Entitlement linking steps (Redwood Console)**
   - Where to go in Console (Marketplace onboarding wizard)
   - How to link subscription to an existing org vs create new
   - What to expect for activation time (set expectation range; do not promise immediate)

4) **Verification steps**
   - How to confirm entitlement is active in Console (entitlement state UI)
   - Optional: run a basic API call / health check
   - Where to see usage/billing view (what is shown vs not shown in Redwood vs AWS)

5) **Troubleshooting**
   - Entitlement not showing up / still pending
   - Linked to wrong org
   - Region mismatch (subscription vs configured region)
   - Multiple AWS accounts / multiple subscriptions
   - Who to contact and what info to include

### FAQ section
Short, procurement-friendly answers. Must align with the Marketplace Security FAQ and approved wording.
Suggested questions:
- How does AWS Marketplace billing work vs direct contract?
- Can we apply committed spend / EDP credits (if applicable, keep high level)?
- Can we upgrade/downgrade SKUs?
- How do refunds/cancellations work?
- What data is sent to AWS as part of metering? (high level)
- Security basics: encryption, audit logs, SSO/SAML (link out to Security FAQ; avoid repeating long content)

### Security/compliance wording constraints
- Do not invent certifications, regions, or retention durations.
- Keep claims scoped to what is true for Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private.
- Any mention of SOC 2 / ISO should be phrased as "available under NDA" and link to the security packet request process where applicable.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AWS Marketplace docs page published and accessible without auth
- [ ] Page includes purchase steps, linking steps, verification, troubleshooting, and FAQ
- [ ] Links added from Pricing and Getting Started pages, with no broken links
- [ ] Security review completed for any security/compliance language (Marcus Lin or Aisha Rahman delegate)
- [ ] Support review completed for troubleshooting steps + contact instructions (Dev Patel)
- [ ] SEO/title metadata set ("Buy Redwood Inference via AWS Marketplace" or similar)

## Analytics (nice-to-have)
Add tracking events or basic page analytics tag (whatever docs site supports) so Growth can monitor visits + click-through to Console.

## References
- PRD: confluence/product-docs/requirements/cloud-marketplace-listing-refresh-prd
- Design spec: confluence/product-docs/design-specs/marketplace-purchase-to-provisioning-onboarding-flow
- Messaging framework: confluence/sales-enablement/positioning-and-messaging/marketplace-listing-messaging-framework
- Support guide draft: confluence/customer-success-and-support/integration-guides/marketplace-provisioning-and-troubleshooting-guide

## Notes
Keep AWS-specific differences explicit and avoid conflating with GCP flow (separate ticket ENG-4405 handles GCP page).
comments: 2025-02-06 (Kira Thompson): Drafted initial outline for /marketplace/aws page. Question: do we want to lead with "Subscribe" or "Link subscription"? I’m leaning subscribe-first, then link, but SE feedback suggests many buyers already subscribed and just need the linking steps.

2025-02-07 (Markus Klein): +1 to making "Already purchased? Link your subscription" very prominent at the top. This is the #1 confusion in calls. Also please include a list of info to send Support (AWS account ID, subscription ID if available, Redwood org slug).

2025-02-10 (Elliot Price): Updated requirements: add a short comparison callout linking to GCP page once live, but keep AWS page self-contained. Also add explicit expectation: entitlement propagation can take some time; don’t promise "instant". Coordinate with Ethan/Cole on realistic ranges.

2025-02-12 (Ethan Park): For expectation language: we usually see entitlements in minutes, but can be delayed. Suggest wording: "typically within ~15 minutes; if longer than 60 minutes, contact Support". Also note that webhook retries are in place but can be impacted by AWS event delays.

2025-02-13 (Marcus Lin): Security wording review notes: (1) Avoid "end-to-end encryption"; say "encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest". (2) Don’t claim customer-managed KMS for Hosted unless explicitly configured/available; keep it as "KMS integrations available for Dedicated/Private". (3) For SOC 2: "SOC 2 report available under NDA upon request"; don’t link to the report directly.

2025-02-14 (Dev Patel): Troubleshooting section additions: include "linked to wrong org" remediation steps and set expectation on what Support can do vs what requires customer admin action. Also include region mismatch symptoms (Console shows entitlement active but model deployment fails in selected region).

2025-02-18 (Kira Thompson): Implemented edits from Marcus/Dev. Added top-of-page CTA boxes: "Already subscribed? Link now" and "New purchase? Subscribe first". Added info checklist for Support tickets. Added links from Pricing and Getting Started pages (pending review).

2025-02-19 (Soojin Lee): Copy tweaks: replace "procurement" with "purchasing" in headers; keep tone developer-first. Added small value prop block: consolidated billing + committed spend. Please avoid mentioning any specific AWS programs unless Legal/Finance ok it.

2025-02-20 (Laura Bennett): Finance note: ok to say "Many customers use AWS Marketplace to apply committed spend" but do not mention EDP by name. Refund/cancellation language should defer to AWS Marketplace terms and Redwood Support for product-side deprovisioning.

2025-02-21 (Kira Thompson): Opened docs PR with the AWS marketplace page + link updates + FAQ (awaiting approvals). Added canonical link + title metadata. Requested final security sign-off on the FAQ section.

2025-02-24 (Elliot Price): Merged and published. Verified links from Pricing and Getting Started. Added note in internal enablement that this is the canonical AWS onboarding doc to send prospects. Closing.
